Follow-up to #305. CodeRabbit's review of 35b3536 left three non-blocking edge cases in `scripts/published-document-links.ts`. The audit should treat Markdown the way GitHub renders it: skip code spans and code blocks, read destinations with nested balanced parentheses, and handle a reference title that starts on the next line. Consider reusing a CommonMark-compliant parser rather than extending the hand-written matcher:

- [scripts/published-document-links.ts:44](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/pull/305#discussion_r4546020638): Exclude code text before checking destinations.
- [scripts/published-document-links.ts:48](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/pull/305#discussion_r4546020649): Read destinations with nested balanced parentheses.
- [scripts/published-document-links.ts:49](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/pull/305#discussion_r4546020658): Include a reference title that starts on the next line.

Each fix needs a test that fails on revert.
Follow-up to #305: Markdown edge cases in the published document link audit

value.text: The Greptile env-PATH deferral is resolved in PR #305 round 6, matching the owner correction here. The nested test environment now prepends the actual Node executable directory to the explicit PATH without inheriting other PM variables. A real non-system Node fixture reproduces failure when only PATH forwarding is reverted, completes promptly with the fix, and passes with Node 22. Public CI evidence: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/actions/runs/43181118299/job/131057054329 . The Markdown follow-ups remain open and unchanged; this entry records only the resolved PATH portion.
